summary: Rogue River NF lookout: first L-4 tower c.1932, replaced by a 30-ft tower in 1946 or 1947, last used in the 1980s, NRHP 2000, NHLR 2003.

facts.design: L-4 cab; original 20-foot timber tower (c.1932), replaced by a 30-foot treated timber L-4 tower

staffing.status: last used in the 1980s; on standby per NHLR, abandoned per firelookout.com

events.note: Site selected and work started, per a Rogue River National Forest history quoted by Forest Lookouts
First lookout: 20-foot timber tower with L-4 cab; NHLR says it went into service in 1932; Forest Lookouts says c.1932
Aircraft Warning Service station activated August 11, 1942
Aircraft Warning Service station deactivated June 14, 1943
30-foot treated timber L-4 tower; firelookout.com dates it to 1946, NHLR says 1947
Approximate year: NHLR says standby since the mid 1980s; firelookout.com says last used in the 1980s
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places; NPGallery record dated 12/29/2000
National Historic Lookout Register registration date March 31, 2003

evidence.supports: First lookout was an L-4 on a 20-foot tower, in service in 1932
evidence.quote: went into service as an L-4 on a 20’ pole tower in 1932

evidence.supports: Replacement with a 30-foot treated timber tower, dated 1947 by NHLR
evidence.quote: In 1947 it was replaced by a newer model L-4 on a 30’ treated timber tower.
It has been on standby status since the mid 1980s.

evidence.supports: About 14 miles west of Crater Lake
30-foot tower built in 1946, last used in the 1980s, now abandoned
evidence.quote: this 30' treated timber L-4 tower, built in 1946, was last used in the 1980's. It is presently abandoned.

evidence.supports: Site selected and work started in 1931
evidence.quote: The site for Stella Mountain Lookout was selected and work started there.

evidence.supports: Original 20-foot native timber tower with L-4 hip-roof cab, c.1932
evidence.quote: c.1932: A 20-foot native timber tower with an L-4 hip-roof cab erected.

evidence.supports: A 1943 newspaper named Mount Stella as a post for a woman lookout
evidence.quote: who will serve as lookout on Mt. Stella

evidence.supports: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, start date 2000
evidence.quote: National Register of Historic Places listed place start time 29 December 2000

evidence.supports: First lookout was a 20-foot L-4 tower, established in 1932
evidence.quote: Established in 1932 with a 20' wooden L-4 tower

corrections.proposed: 1932 built (first 20-foot L-4 tower); 30-foot replacement in 1946 or 1947
corrections.why: NHLR's own description says the L-4 went into service in 1932 and that 1947 was the replacement; firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts also date the first tower to c.1932.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the 30-foot replacement to 1947 and firelookout.com dates it to 1946. Both are kept, and the story says the year is disputed.
NHLR says the lookout has been on standby since the mid 1980s; firelookout.com says it was last used in the 1980s and is presently abandoned. The story reports both.

sources.title: Mt. Stella Lookout
sources.publisher: National Register of Historic Places, NPGallery

notes_for_editor: The record's 'built 1947' is the replacement date; the first tower is 1932 per NHLR text, firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts. Access is not stated by any source read, so no access level is given. Elevation differs across sources (NHLR 4,665 ft, firelookout.com 4715 ft, Wikidata 4,695 ft) and the record's 1421.9 m was left alone. Staffing as_of is the NHLR 'mid 1980s' wording because the pages are undated. Cherylhill.net also gives 1946 for the replacement but was not fetched.
